clue.text: Complete with runners in high spirits

parts.note: something complete with a feature is full of it
runner beans are a climbing vegetable, so runners are beans

explanation.surface: A sprinter, kitted out with a team of runners, is in an excellent mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners' suggests athletes, but here it means runner beans, a common British garden vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bursting with energy and cheer is the idiom's meaning, a lively, exuberant mood.

clue.text: Ventilator to suit groups of supporters

parts.note: a fan is a device that moves air, a ventilator
clubs is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: An air-conditioning unit chosen to match the decor pleases bands of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: Organised societies of admirers of a star or team are exactly what these supporters' groups are called.

clue.text: 50-1 pussyfoot has spoken by the shore …

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one
a pussyfoot is a teetotaller (after the US prohibitionist 'Pussyfoot' Johnson), abbreviated TT
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A rank outsider at long odds, a cautious type, has talked down at the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: '50-1' reads as betting odds but is the Roman numerals L and I; 'pussyfoot' as a noun once meant a teetotaller, hence TT.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things on or near the coast, the strip of land beside the sea.

clue.text: so as I can renovate deserted refuge

indicators.note: to renovate is to rebuild or remake, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Continuing the seaside theme, someone hopes to restore an abandoned shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues the previous one after its ellipsis, and 'can' is only a link. 'deserted' means in a desert, not abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile watered spot in a desert is a haven for travellers, a refuge in the sands.

clue.text: Stop girl pump attendant

parts.note: to bar is to stop or block
a maid is an old word for a girl

explanation.surface: Halt the young woman who works at the petrol station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pump attendant' suggests a petrol station, but the pump here is a beer pump in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: She pulls pints at the beer engine's handles, so she tends the pumps behind a pub counter.

clue.text: A right one getting his teeth into umpire

parts.note: someone who bites, a biter

explanation.surface: A fair-minded man sinks his teeth into the referee.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a judge appointed to settle disputes or decide a contest.

clue.text: Air revolution in vocal series

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
a cycle is one full turn, a revolution

explanation.surface: A tune of change appears in a run of sung performances.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of songs meant to be performed in sequence forms a sung series, as by Schubert.

clue.text: Stuff for the bed-sitter

explanation.definitionFit: To stuff or cushion something is to pad it; a pad is slang for a home, such as a one-room flat.

clue.text: Supply forgotten words ready for delivery

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre helper feeds an actor missing lines; punctual and ready to deliver promptly also describes something done at once.

clue.text: Artful character playing' in Brooklyn

explanation.walkthrough: The Brooklyn baseball team moved to Los Angeles in 1958; one member of it is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Artful nickname belongs to a pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist; a baseball club once played in Brooklyn under that team name.

clue.text: Money-making music

explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are paper money; written musical symbols, or the tones they stand for, are music.

clue.text: Outlaw used to steal wearing cover for head

parts.note: to rob is to steal from
someone wearing a garment is in it
a hood covers the head

explanation.surface: A bandit's trick to commit theft is to put on a balaclava.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary bandit of Sherwood Forest is the archetypal English outlaw.

clue.text: Appears to auction room to be quick

parts.note: to look is to appear or seem
a mart is a market or auction room

explanation.surface: Someone seems to dash off to the saleroom in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an urging to hurry up, chiefly British, meaning move fast.

clue.text: Police heard in wood

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken and we take the word that sounds like it

parts.note: cops is slang for police

explanation.surface: Officers' voices are audible among the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thicket of trees is a little wood.

clue.text: Committee newsman got on

parts.note: a board is a governing committee
ED is the usual short form of editor, a newspaperman

explanation.surface: A member of the panel and a journalist climbed aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on a ship, bus or plane is to embark on it, to climb aboard.

clue.text: Bathes fascinating female light controller

parts.note: to dip is to bathe briefly
a witch casts spells, so she fascinates in the old sense of bewitching

explanation.surface: A captivating woman takes a swim, a glamorous picture.
explanation.walkthrough: A dipswitch on a car flips the headlights between full and dipped beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A car headlamp beam is lowered by this switch, so it controls lights.

clue.text: Music from one of the Stones

explanation.definitionFit: Rock is a genre of popular music; a single stone or pebble is also a rock.

clue.text: I would upset effort to seize goods in default

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would
strain is great effort

explanation.surface: Someone would object to the hard work needed to repossess goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ID upside down to DI in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal term means taking a debtor's property to cover unpaid money owed.

clue.text: Southern drudge showed the way in bonds

parts.note: a hack is someone who does dull work
led means guided, showed the way

explanation.surface: A labourer from the south led others into captivity.
explanation.definitionFit: Being chained or fettered means held in restraints, tied up.

clue.text: Circle piano with useless work from composer

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
US is short for unserviceable, meaning useless

explanation.surface: A ring and a keyboard instrument, useless for a composer's labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition is numbered in a composer's catalogue by this Latin word meaning a work.

clue.text: Keener cheat

explanation.definitionFit: Sharper means more acute or eager; a sharper is a swindler, especially at cards.

clue.text: Fault in' limb he's broken

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: An injury to someone's arm or leg is a defect.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain or flaw spoils something's perfection, a defect.

clue.text: Female supporter goes to northern bath for lucky dip

parts.note: a bra supports a woman's bust
a tub is a bath

explanation.surface: A woman who backs the team heads north to take a bath and try her luck.
explanation.walkthrough: A bran tub is a British fairground game: a tub of bran with hidden prizes to dig for.
explanation.definitionFit: The fete game has players rummaging for a hidden prize, the same game as a lucky dip.

clue.text: Chap creating bad visibility

explanation.definitionFit: Mister is a form of address for a man; a thing that makes a fine spray or fog would be a mister.

clue.text: Continue to signal bottle

parts.note: to flag is to signal, as with a flag
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: Keep on waving for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A large vessel for wine or cider with a handle is a kind of bottle.

clue.text: Relation picked up after the match

definitions.text: Relation picked up after the match

parts.words: Relation picked up after the match
parts.note: a match is a marriage, and marrying brings a spouse's family members as new relatives

explanation.surface: A relative turns up after the football game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a sports fixture, but it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage creates kin by law, the spouse's parents and siblings.

clue.text: Not interested in a sad .

parts.note: pathetic means sad or pitiful

explanation.surface: Indifferent to an unhappy drunk, the clue leads into the next one.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 26 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking concern or enthusiasm is to be indifferent, without interest.

clue.text: Monster that never lost its head

definitions.text: Monster that never lost its head

parts.words: Monster that never lost its head
parts.note: in Greek myth this many-headed serpent grew two new heads for each one cut off

explanation.surface: A creature that always kept calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never lost its head' sounds like staying calm, but Heracles cutting off heads never left this beast headless.
explanation.definitionFit: The serpent of Lerna, slain by Heracles, is a mythical many-headed beast.

clue.text: … drunk getting to notice awkward situation

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
to spot is to notice

explanation.surface: Getting drunk enough to be noticed leads to an embarrassing predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult predicament is a fix, a tough corner to be in.

clue.text: Doctor comes to boring bit of speech

parts.note: an awl is a tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: The physician comes to the dull part of an address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull, but means drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow, lazy manner of talking with long vowels is a way of speech.

clue.text: Manage to back united railmen

indicators.note: back means read from end to start, a reversal

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone tries to support the railway workers' union.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUR, Britain's National Union of Railwaymen, read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business is to manage it.

clue.text: Crazy having animal beaten to death

parts.note: a hare is an animal
to brain someone is to kill them with a blow to the head

explanation.surface: A mad scheme involves a creature being clubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish, reckless and silly, a wild scheme is called this.
